summary: Andorra requires no visa of any kind and has no airport: it is reached through France or Spain, so Schengen rules decide who can come. EU/EEA citizens and Schengen visa-free nationalities can travel there freely, while travelers who need a Schengen visa must hold a double- or multiple-entry one, because Andorra is outside the Schengen Area.

Travelers who need a Schengen visa to reach Andorra through France or Spain must hold the travel medical insurance the visa requires (minimum EUR 30,000 cover). The UK government says the EHIC and GHIC are not valid in Andorra and advises taking out comprehensive travel and medical insurance before travelling.

tips.text: If you needed a visa to enter the Schengen Area, the Government of Canada advises holding a multiple-entry visa before visiting Andorra: Andorra is outside Schengen, and holders of a single-entry visa may be refused re-entry to France or Spain.
Andorra is landlocked and has no airport, according to the Government of Canada; you must enter through France or Spain.
France and Spain apply strict limits on the tobacco and alcohol you bring out of Andorra for personal use. The UK FCDO says customs officers may impound excess tobacco and the vehicle carrying it.
From 1 November to 15 May you must use winter tyres or carry snow chains in Andorra, and you can be fined if you do not (UK FCDO).

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Andorra?
faq.answer: Andorra's government says the Principality does not require any type of visa. Entry is governed by Schengen rules because you must pass through France or Spain: EU/EEA citizens and Schengen visa-free nationalities (US, UK, Japan and many more) need no visa, and if your passport needs a Schengen visa, the Andorran government says to get a double- or multiple-entry one so you can re-enter France or Spain afterward.

faq.question: Does time in Andorra count against my 90-day Schengen allowance?
faq.answer: Andorra's government says the Principality is not a member of the Schengen Area, and the Schengen 90-day limit counts stays on the territory of the Schengen states.

faq.question: Can I visit Andorra on a single-entry Schengen visa?
faq.answer: Andorra's government says travellers who need a Schengen visa must apply for a double- or multiple-entry one, and Canada's travel advice says holders of a single-entry visa will face delays and may be refused re-entry when returning to France or Spain.

faq.question: How do I get to Andorra without an airport?
faq.answer: By road, through France or Spain: Andorra has no airport (Government of Canada). From 1 November to 15 May, winter tyres or snow chains are compulsory on Andorran roads (UK FCDO).

faq.question: What currency does Andorra use?
faq.answer: The euro. According to the European Commission, Andorra is not in the euro area but has a monetary agreement with the EU that makes the euro its official currency.
